statement: A train 160 m long travels at 72 km/h and crosses a bridge 440 m long. How many seconds pass from the moment the front of the train reaches the bridge until the back of the train leaves it?

choices.misconception: I only used the length of the train, 160 m, as the distance travelled.
I subtracted the train's length from the bridge, 440 - 160 = 280 m, as if the train only had to be wholly on the bridge.
I used only the bridge's 440 m and forgot that the train must also travel its own length to clear it.
I changed 72 km/h into metres per second by dividing by 60 only, getting 1.2 m/s instead of 20 m/s.

hints: Follow the back of the train: how far does it travel?
Put the speed into metres per second first. The front must cross the whole bridge, and then the rest of the train must follow it off.
72 km/h is 72 000 m in 3600 s, which is 20 m/s, and the distance is 160 + 440 = 600 m.

solutions.reliable: 72 km/h = 72 000 m / 3600 s = 20 m/s. From the front reaching the bridge to the back leaving it, the back of the train travels the length of the bridge plus the length of the train, 440 + 160 = 600 m. The time is 600 / 20 = 30 seconds. The transferable idea: convert to matching units before dividing, and track one fixed point on a moving object to see the real distance.

whyOnTest: Unit conversion and reading exactly which moment ends the crossing decide this, and each distractor is a slip in one of the two.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
